description_full: Qfin Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operate AI- driven credit-tech platform under the Qifu Jietiao brand in the People's Republic of China. The company provides credit-driven services that match borrowers with financial institutions to conduct borrower acquisition, credit assessment, fund matching, and post-facilitation services; and platform services, including loan and post-facilitation services to financial institution partners under capital light model, intelligence credit engine, referral services, and other technology solutions. It serves financial institutions, consumers, and small and micro-enterprises. The company was formerly known as Qifu Technology, Inc. and changed its name to Qfin Holdings, Inc. in July 2025. Qfin Holdings, Inc. was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in Shanghai, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: Qfin Holdings, Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $646M market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 36% against a 10% cost of capital — a 26-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $1.6B in free cash flow — roughly 56 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.85× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

sector_headwinds.text: Altman Z in the grey zone — financial health warrants monitoring
Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.
Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

sect: Its 35% operating margin runs 6pp above the Financial Services median (29%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 514 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 72% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 77% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 56% and a beta of 1.06, it moves roughly with the market.
About $13.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 40% in the 2020 crash and 55% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 96% below its DCF fair value of $130, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 11%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $108 to $161 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Financial Services peers: P/E 1.3 vs 12.3 and P/FCF 0.4 vs 13.0 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 72% below its 10-year median.
The 12 covering analysts target $14.29 on average, 169% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 36% clears the cost of capital of 9.9% by 26pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.39).
It converts 56% of revenue into free cash flow.
It earns a 25% return on equity.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 2.7% over 3 years and 6.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 35%).
At current returns, reinvesting 93% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has missed earnings estimates by 13.7% on average.
Analysts expect 4.6% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.4%, and institutions hold 67%.
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 3 sales over the past year, net $2.4M sold.
The share count has shrunk 4.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 3,557 employees, each generates about $810K of revenue, 1.6x the Financial Services median, and revenue has grown 21.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $458K of free cash flow per employee.
